item.title: Kyoto Railway Museum: Steam Trains to Shinkansen — Guide
item.description: The Kyoto Railway Museum, opened in 2016 just west of Kyoto Station, is one of the best railway museums in Japan and a superb outing for families and enthusiasts alike. It displays 53 real trains spanning the whole history of Japanese rail, from black steam locomotives through classic express carriages to an early shinkansen bullet train, many of which you can board. A highlight is the preserved roundhouse and turntable, where working steam locomotives are still kept, and you can ride a genuine steam train on a short line.

item.title: Isumi Railway Guide: Rapeseed Flowers, Trains & Access
item.description: The Isumi Railway is one of Chiba’s most photogenic country railways — a single-carriage local line winding through the rural heart of the Boso Peninsula. It’s most famous in spring, when the tracks are framed by ribbons of golden rapeseed blossom (nanohana) and pink cherry trees, drawing photographers to capture the little train rolling through a sea of yellow. Cute themed services (including Moomin-decorated trains and a dining “restaurant train”) add to the charm.
